newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Normal winter temps for Brazil coffee areas - Somar.
newsitem.headline: Normal winter temps for Brazil coffee areas - Somar.

text.p: Brazil's southwest which includes the coffee states of Minas Gerais, Sao Paulo, Espirito Santo and north Parana should mainly see seasonal temperatures in April to June, said local forecaster Somar Meteorologia.
Only in the north of Minas should temperatures fall slightly below normal levels for this time of year, it added in a regular outlook.
"The same pattern should carry on throughout the winter," said Marcos Massari, forecaster at Somar.

Rainfall should be marginally below average in Minas Gerais, Rio de Janeiro, Espirito Santo and the north/northeast of Sao Paulo. The remainder of Sao Paulo state should see normal rainfall during April, May and June.
Massari warned "normal" temperatures were colder than those seen over the past four years which have been affected by the "El Nino" and "La Nina" weather phenomena.
"In the last four years, temperatures have been above average," Massari said.
June, July and August traditionally pose the greatest frost threat to Brazilian coffee trees although concern over low temperatures usually begins in May.

The country's trees should virtually have recovered from two sharp frosts in 1994 which practically wiped out production in some areas and expectations are already of a super crop in 1998, weather permiting.
